ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: A Lightweight Dual-Branch Visual Front-End for Efficient Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.36834v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction (AVTSE) uses face-related visual cues to extract a target speaker from a speech mixture. In many AVTSE systems, visual features are obtained from convolutional image encoders, and their computation may become a non-negligible part of the overall system when lightweight separation backbones are used. This work proposes a dual-branch visual front-end that reorganizes visual information according to its spatial characteristics. A compact lip region of interest is used to model local articulation cues through c

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.36892v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech enhancement (SE) systems are commonly evaluated with objective metrics, with and without references, and with categorical subjective listening tests, all measuring speech quality and intelligibility. So far, it is unclear from such evaluations whether the processed speech is perceptually different or is preferred by everyday listeners. We investigate discrimination and preference as complementary dimensions of SE evaluation through crowdsourced triangle and pairwise preference tests across four SE systems, with comparisons to clean refere

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: StreamSE: Neural Audio Codec-based Streaming Speech Enhancement for On-device Inference
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.37024v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent generative speech enhancement (SE) models achieve high perceptual quality, but their non-causal processing and expensive computation make them difficult to use for streaming, on-device inference. We propose StreamSE, a 20M-parameter streaming SE model that operates in the latent space of a frozen pretrained neural audio codec. At each frame, StreamSE directly regresses a clean continuous latent from the noisy continuous latent while conditioning on its own predictions from previous frames. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.36713v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Personalized spoken agents must identify speakers before accessing user-specific memory, yet memory benchmarks typically assume correctly attributed histories. We argue that voiceprints are observations of identity, not identities themselves, and formulate online speaker-memory construction to maintain persistent user entities as acoustic evidence evolves. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.36715v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Neural music editing requires a system to perform a requested change while preserving the musical content that should remain unchanged. Existing evaluations often lack a paired target edit, making these requirements difficult to measure separately. We introduce SMEBench, a large-scale benchmark of controlled music edits constructed by modifying symbolic MIDI performances and rendering matched source and target audio. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.36911v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Although the recent development of LLMs has paved the way for multi-modal interaction, minority languages face difficulties keeping pace. This work presents the first open Speech Language Model for Basque, designed for low-latency, end-to-end spoken interaction. Based on the LLaMA-Omni architecture, the system integrates a Latxa model as its backbone, transferring its Basque capabilities to the spoken modality by fine-tuning several modules. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.37640v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Recent advances in generative audio models facilitate increasingly flexible and selective editing of linguistic content and paralinguistic, extralinguistic, and other attributes. This paradigm, named partially edited audio, differs from full audio generation as only portions of the real recording are edited. This technique can serve both beneficial and harmful applications. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Integrated Spoofing-Robust Automatic Speaker Verification via a Three-Class Formulation and LLR
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2603.13780v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Spoofing-robust automatic speaker verification (SASV) aims to integrate automatic speaker verification (ASV) and countermeasure (CM). A popular solution is fusion of independent ASV and CM scores. To better modeling SASV, some frameworks integrate ASV and CM within a single network. However, these solutions are typically bi-encoder based, offer limited interpretability, and cannot be readily adapted to new evaluation parameters without retraining. Based on this, we propose a unified end-to-end framework via a three-class formulation that ena

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Sonifying I2S Transport Signals to Detect Transmission Faults
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2608.16498v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper outlines a sonification design to support fault detection in the transmission of I2S transport signals. I2S is a protocol for communicating real-time digital audio between integrated circuits that, while in wide and general use, does not include built-in error detection. Moreover, given the nature of the protocol transmission faults affecting timing, framing and alignment can be difficult to identify using conventional visual methods. The proposed design addresses this with an approach informed by Audification, wherein oversamplin

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: AzeroS: Extending LLM to Speech with Self-Generated Instruction-Free Tuning
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2601.06086v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Extending large language models (LLMs) to the speech domain has recently gained significant attention. A typical approach connects a pretrained LLM with an audio encoder through a projection module and trains the resulting model on large-scale, task-specific instruction-tuning datasets. However, curating such instruction-tuning data for specific requirements is time-consuming, and models trained in this manner often generalize poorly to unseen tasks. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: A Benchmark for Controllable Speaking-Style Captioning in Audio-Language Models
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.33036v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Speaking-style captioning (SSC) aims to generate natural language descriptions of how speech is delivered, capturing paralinguistic attributes such as vocal timbre, prosody, and expressivity. Many downstream applications, including conversational AI agents, controllable speech generation, and large-scale audio annotation, require dimension-specific style captions that describe targeted aspects of speech (e.g., speaker traits, emotion, or delivery style), rather than a single undifferentiated description. However, existing work lacks a

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Correspondence Is Not Transfer: A Pairing-Controlled Study of Clinical Audio-Metadata Alignment
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.35747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Clinical audio models are often trained by aligning recordings with participant metadata or text derived from it. This metadata is rarely a clean disease signal, since a single profile also contains symptoms, age, sex, missing responses, and recruitment information. We examine what alignment adds to frozen audio features by varying only the audio-meta data pairing. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.36126v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate prediction of human Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) is crucial for evaluating synthetic speech quality in text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC). Most MOS predictors output only point estimates and ignore uncertainty, limiting reliability in model selection and deployment. We propose ConformalMOS, a framework that augments MOS prediction with conformal prediction to produce statistically valid prediction intervals with guaranteed coverage under exchangeability, alongside point estimates. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: TAC2: Timestamped Audio Captioning as composable functions
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.36568v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Real-world audio applications require precise, queryable representations grounded in physical time. Yet modern Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) increasingly favor conversational generation, producing free-form descriptions that conflate acoustic perception with higher-level reasoning and lack precise temporal grounding. We introduce TAC2, a foundation model that casts timestamped audio captioning as composable functions to construct granular, speaker-attributed acoustic timelines directly from in-the-wild audio. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.36578v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning has made Audio Large Language Models (Audio LLMs) better reasoners, but the reward that drives it still comes from outside the model: a final-answer check, a hand-crafted process score, or an external LLM judge that stays fixed while the policy improves. We show that an Audio LLM can supply this reward itself, and can do so recursively: each improved model becomes the critic that trains its successor, so the training signal improves along with the model. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.36643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction (AV-TSE) uses a target speaker's face to extract the speaker's speech from an input audio mixture in real time. However, existing systems fix the target speaker for an entire clip, while conversation demands frequent and immediate target switches. To address this problem, we propose Tap2Listen, a streaming AV-TSE model designed for instant response to target switches. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: The Content Leash: Mitigating Degenerate Solutions in Invertible Speaker Anonymization
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.36768v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Voice anonymization aims to protect a speaker's identity while preserving the linguistic content of speech, enabling voice data to be shared and processed with reduced privacy risk. This work focuses on reversible voice anonymization, where the original voice can be recovered by an authorized user rather than being permanently discarded. However, existing approaches can achieve apparent speaker anonymization by degrading the speech itself, while their effectiveness may also depend on the speaker-verification representation used during training.

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: S3-S2ST: Semantically Supervised Streaming Speech-to-Speech Translation
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.36777v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Streaming speech-to-speech translation requires timely decisions about when partial input is sufficient for accurate translation. We present S3-S2ST, a model that learns to translate and speak from semantically aligned streaming supervision. By converting utterance-level speech pairs into incremental training examples, we teach a learned policy when to commit translations. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.36786v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Realistic guitar synthesis requires both audio fidelity and interpretable control over how notes are performed. The input timed MIDI events decide what is played but not how, leaving the continuous within-note decisions of guitar performance--such as pitch inflection and per-string articulation--unspecified. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.36865v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio systems aim to maximise the listener's perceived quality, traditionally evaluated through mean opinion scoring (MOS), a subjective process that is slow, costly, and collected only after playback. Machine learning now predicts MOS directly from the audio, but in generalising across participants it tends to discard the subject variance that defines individual perception. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.37083v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tracheal auscultation is recommended by clinical practice guidelines, and required by some U.S. state regulations, for monitoring ventilation during procedural sedation and monitored anesthesia care. However, continuous auscultation with a conventional stethoscope is impractical, susceptible to ambient noise, and difficult to interpret. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: EEG-Based Decoding of Musical Mode and Melodic Direction Using Empirical Mode Decomposition
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.37148v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has proven to be a powerful tool for decoding neural activity in real-life scenarios, including the perception and processing of emotions elicited by music. Among the various musical features that modulate these responses, musical mode and melodic direction (or contour) play a central role. This work proposes a novel EEG feature extraction framework based on Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to decompose EEG signals recorded during active piano performance for the detection of these two musical features. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.37270v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The hybrid work trend in the post-COVID period has transformed how people communicate while at work. However, there is a lack of quantitative understanding of how home and office environments shape communicative behavior and affective well-being. To study this, as a part of a larger study of the role of work environment on stress, we designed an egocentric wearable audio sensing system that captured interpersonal communication across both working locations. CDM — Create Digital Music.title: On the sublime BETHLEHEM بيت لحم, walls in time and space fall
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
The exquisite collaboration of Lawrence Sammour, Sary Moussa, and Abed Kobeissy, Bethlehem, is released this month. And it has become a rich sanctuary, a shared space that refuses erasure or fragmentation. It also refuses to obey the boundaries of colonialism and occupation, weaving together what was pulled apart, as taut and resonant as the strings of the buzuq.
